criteria.criterion: A test first shows a file edit and a git commit succeed in an unlocked snapshot under the current user, then shows both are refused once the verifier's lock/grant is applied, and that HEAD and work-tree tree are unchanged. It fails (not skips or returns early) if the write is not refused. Run: cargo test -p athena-git and cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: snapshot.rs has two tests: an_unlocked_snapshot_takes_edits_and_commits asserts (true,true,true) and that HEAD moved; a_locked_snapshot_refuses_edits_and_commits_and_keeps_head_and_tree calls lock().expect(...) and asserts (false,false,false), then checks that HEAD and the tree are unchanged and that unlocking makes writes work again. There is no early return, and lock() errors when its write probe succeeds. Both tests passed here under root. The rest of athena-core passed too, including a_verifier_write_is_refused_by_the_lock_and_does_not_reach_the_work.

criteria.criterion: The verifier-grant write deny is tested in policy: a write tool call against the snapshot path is denied even when the process is root. Run: cargo test -p athena-agent.
criteria.evidence: the_verifier_grant_denies_every_write_to_the_snapshot_whoever_runs_it first shows the process can open the file for writing. It then asserts that Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit and write-type bash commands are denied under the verifier grant, and that the same Edit is allowed under the producer grant as a control. The test passed in this run, which was under root because the working directory is under ~.

criteria.criterion: A fake-agent test shows a changed snapshot fingerprint after the first verifier run triggers exactly one more verifier invocation on a freshly created snapshot, and the first verdict is discarded. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: a_verifier_that_changed_its_snapshot_is_rerun_once_on_a_fresh_one_and_the_fault_is_recorded asserts exactly 2 runs and that the second run began without the tampered file, i.e. on a fresh snapshot. It also checks that the first run's fail verdict was discarded: the job landed with the second run's summary 'Fine.'. The test passed.

criteria.criterion: A test shows that after a changed fingerprint the outcome is recorded as a system fault and the judgment has no 'verifier changed its snapshot' blocker and does not reject the work; an unchanged snapshot runs the verifier once and uses its verdict. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: The rerun test asserts one Minor 'System fault' finding, no 'changed its snapshot, which invalidates' finding, and the Landed state. verify.rs test a_system_fault_is_recorded_and_never_rejects_the_work checks the same at the judge level. an_unchanged_snapshot_runs_the_verifier_once_and_uses_its_verdict asserts 1 run, no fault, and the 'Fine.' verdict. All passed.

criteria.criterion: A test shows that when the budget is exhausted before the rerun, the job's reason reports the budget failure rather than 'snapshot changed twice'. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: when_the_budget_runs_out_before_the_rerun_the_reason_reports_the_budget asserts 1 run, a reason containing 'budget left', and a reason containing neither 'twice' nor 'both runs'. It passed.

criteria.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test pass on the workspace.
criteria.evidence: Athena reports that fmt, clippy (-D warnings) and the workspace tests (668) passed on this tree. I re-ran the athena-git, athena-agent and athena-core tests: all passed, 0 failed.

criteria.criterion: verify.rs no longer turns snapshot_changed into a blocker against the work, and run.rs near the old snapshot_changed branch discards the verdict and reruns once.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: in verify.rs, snapshot_changed is replaced by system_fault, which yields a Minor finding and no reason, and the pass condition no longer depends on it. In run.rs, the old branch now clears verdict_output, verifier_failure, commands_run and verifier_invocation, builds a fresh snapshot with verifier_snapshot(), and stops after the second run.

findings.summary: If the verifier changes its snapshot on both runs, the job is still Rejected.
findings.evidence: When both runs change the snapshot, verifier_failure is set, so judge() adds 'the verifier did not complete' and the test asserts OutcomeState::Rejected. No blocker is raised against the work, but the reading says a system fault is recorded 'instead of rejecting the work'. A distinct non-rejecting state for this case may be wanted later.

findings.summary: Unlocking gives the pinned read-only tree its write bit back.
findings.evidence: set_tree_writable(dir, true) walks into the pinned copy that pin::mount made read-only and adds the owner write bit. This is harmless now, because no agent uses the snapshot after the verifier runs, but it undoes the mount's read-only state.

findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs is listed as a deliverable but was not changed.
findings.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1 --stat -- crates/athena-cli` prints nothing. No criterion requires a change there, and no file outside the deliverables list was touched.

summary: The change does what the reading asks, and I recommend it pass. The verifier's snapshot is now protected two ways: the grant's write deny, tested in policy.rs to hold even though the test process could write the file itself, and a new Snapshot::lock. The lock removes write bits and adds the immutable attribute via chattr, then probes with a real write and errors if the write still works, so the tests fail rather than skip. If the snapshot still changes, run.rs throws away that verdict, reruns the verifier once on a fresh snapshot, and records a Minor system-fault finding instead of a blocker against the work. When the budget runs out first, the reason names the budget. I ran cargo test for athena-git, athena-agent and athena-core: every new test passed, including the unlocked-versus-locked control pair (run as root), the rerun, the unchanged-snapshot case, the twice-changed case and the budget case. These results come from the snapshot only. Remaining points: if the snapshot changes on both runs the job is still Rejected (minor), unlocking makes the pinned tree writable again (nit), and lifecycle.rs was listed as a deliverable but not changed (nit).
